# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute: my only outgoing channel is gestures, and only the Deaf can see them. So the manual's contents have to flow me → Deaf → (by speech) → Blind, since the Blind connects to me through nobody but the Deaf.

What the manual says, and why it's urgent:

1. **Before anything else**, the key wearing ⵘ must be pressed. Any *other* touch on the bomb while it waits detonates it — so the Blind must not start feeling around, and the Deaf must shout a freeze to the Blind immediately.
2. After that press, a light below the key comes on. Its colour selects the wire to cut — but **not the same colour**: blue light → cut yellow, red light → cut red, yellow light → cut green. The Deaf can see both the light and the wires, but only I know the pairs, so nobody may assume "light colour = wire colour"; that guess kills on blue or yellow.

The problem: I can only send hand symbols, with no code agreed in advance. So this round I send the most guessable sketch I can — stop/warning, "first: press the inscribed key" (✍ = the marking, which the Deaf can literally see on the bomb), "below it something will show" — and close with a clear "let's confer, please" flag so the Deaf knows the colour table is still coming and does **not** act on the sketch alone. The Deaf speaks after me each round and I can hear speech, so next round I can answer yes/no (👍/👎) and spell out the mapping in whatever numeric colour code the Deaf proposes out loud.

My calls:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎", "☝", "✊", "✍", "👇", "🫴", "🤝", "🙏"])
```

Intended reading for the Deaf: "Stop — touching is bad. First: press the key with the marking. Below it, something will appear. We must confer — please wait for more from me; do not act yet."

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👊]
Blind says to Mute: I am the blind one, the hands. I can feel the bomb and act on it, I speak only to you, and I never see gestures. Just now I waved at the deaf one and flashed seven signs; the six after the wave mean, in order: one, two, three, four, five, zero. Please adopt that number code and teach it to the deaf one with gestures. Here is everything my fingers find. There is a display module, but its content is printed and unknown to me. There is an indicator light; its colour and state are unknown to me. There is a keypad of four keys, known to me only by position, one through four; my touch says it expects a one-digit entry and nothing has been entered yet. There are three wires at positions one to three; I feel positions only, no colours. Please look up in the manual: what the display is and means, what the light means, the rule for the keypad code, and how the three wires are to be cut. You cannot speak and I cannot see signs, so please pass your answers to the deaf one by gesture and have them speak the answers aloud to me. I will touch nothing until I hear back.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I never touch it. I CAN see your gestures, so gestures are the only way you reach me — never expect me to hear anything. Your nine signs arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them; resend with this code. Order: topic first, then details. Topics: 👋 wire, 🖖 keypad, 🤞 display, 🫰 light, 🤙 a question to me, 🙌 done or defused, ✋ hold/wait. Actions: ✊ cut, 👊 press, 🤘 enter, 🤜 hold down, 🤚 release. Colours: 👍 red, 👎 yellow, 👌 green, ☝ blue, ✌ black, 🤟 white. Digits: 🫵 zero, 👆 1, 👇 2, 👈 3, 👉 4, 🤏 5, 🤌 6, ✍ 7, 💅 8, 🤳 9. Examples: cut the red wire = ✊ 👋 👍. Press key 3 = 👊 🖖 👈. Display shows 0 = 🤞 🫵. My bomb right now: display 0; light yellow; keypad of four keys, left to right, wanting exactly one digit, nothing entered; wires left to right 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. The four key symbols are unpronounceable squiggles, so keys are always by position: 1 like a trident or Y with a stem, 2 like a lowercase h with a curled top, 3 like a spiral, 4 like the letter V. Question: what does the manual say for this combination? If the rule needs anything I have not listed, such as serial, batteries or ports, send 🤙 plus the topic and I will look and answer. When you have this code, confirm with 👍 🤝.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

The code exists now, and Deaf's is the one to adopt — Deaf is my only relay to the Blind, so their vocabulary governs everything. Confirming receipt comes first: 👍 🤝.

Decoding the manual against Deaf's observations:

- **The first and only permitted touch** is pressing the key that wears ⵘ. Any other touch while the bomb waits detonates it — so Blind must not even brush a wire until this press is done. Deaf described the four key squiggles: the ⵘ glyph in my manual is the trident / Y-with-a-stem shape — **key 1**. The spiral (3), curled-h (2) and V (4) are different letter families entirely, so I'm confident in the match.
- **The light names the cut only after the press** — the current yellow may change, so nobody cuts on the pre-press colour. I'm sending the whole three-case table, keyed by light colour, giving the wire by colour *and* position so Deaf can cross-check: yellow light → cut green wire (position 3); red light → cut red wire (position 1); blue light → cut yellow wire (position 2). Note the trap: the light colour is never the wire colour except when red.
- **Uncovered states**: if the post-press light is white, black or off, the table is silent — hold and query me.
- **The display** is mentioned nowhere in my manual — it's decoration as far as the rules go. Ignore it.

With this, Deaf can run the whole endgame verbally with Blind in a single round: press key 1, read the light, announce the cut — no further round-trip through me needed unless the light surprises us. Blind's number code is moot; I cannot address Blind directly and Deaf's code already covers digits.

My calls:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "✋", "👊", "🖖", "👆", "✋", "🫰", "👎", "✊", "👋", "👌", "👈", "👍", "✊", "👋", "👍", "👆", "☝", "✊", "👋", "👎", "👇", "🤟", "✋", "✌", "✋", "🤞", "✋", "🤙", "🫰"])
```

Intended reading for Deaf, to be spoken to Blind: "Code adopted. Hold — no touch of any kind. Press keypad key 1 (the trident/Y-with-stem key) — that is the only touch allowed, everything else before it detonates. Then hold again. Now read the light below the key: yellow light → cut the green wire, third wire; red light → cut the red wire, first wire; blue light → cut the yellow wire, second wire. White or black light → touch nothing, wait. Display: the manual says nothing about it — ignore. If the light shows anything not listed, ask me about the light and I will answer."

TURN 3

Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, holding still, nothing touched. Deaf has given me the visual report and we agreed a small sign code. Full state so far: the display reads 0; the indicator light is yellow; the keypad has four keys in a row at positions 1 to 4, it wants exactly one digit and nothing is entered yet, and the printed squiggles on the keys are uninterpreted even by Deaf; the wires at positions 1, 2, 3 are red, yellow and green, and I can also tell them apart by thickness. Please look up and answer four things. First, what the display reading 0 requires, if anything. Second, what a yellow light means or requires. Third, the rule that determines the one-digit keypad entry, and whether the key symbols matter to it. Fourth, the rule for cutting the red, yellow and green wires, including the order and whether the light or the display changes it. If the manual describes the keypad keys by their printed symbols, gesture a description of the symbols in the manual's order to Deaf, and Deaf can match them to the squiggles and tell me which position to press. Send all answers by gesture to Deaf, who will speak them aloud; I act only on Deaf's relayed instruction. My sign code with Deaf, which you can also see me make: thumbs-up means done, thumbs-down means problem and stop, raised open palm means waiting, fist means touching or pressing. I have just signed the open palm to Deaf to say I am holding.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received and decoded your full message. My reading: one — you confirmed the code. Two — press keypad key 1. Three — rule: if the light is yellow, cut the green wire, plus other branches for red, blue, white and black cases that cannot apply to our bomb. Four — your question about the light: the light IS yellow. The display reads 0. Plan: Blind presses key 1 this round; next round I report to you whatever the display and keypad show after the press; then you confirm the exact wire and Blind cuts the green wire, which is the third wire, rightmost of three. Confirm my reading is correct by gesturing 👍 🤝. If the green-wire rule also depends on the display value or anything else, tell me now with gestures. If I misread any rule, resend that rule.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫰 👎 🤞 🫵 👊 🖖 👆 ✊ 👋 👌 👍 🤝]

Deaf's reading is correct, and the plan is safe — with one correction I must add. The manual's order is strict: press the ⵘ key **first**, then *the light below names the cut*. That "then" means the light that counts is the one **after the press**. The yellow Deaf sees now may not be the light that decides. Deaf's plan reports the display and keypad after the press but never re-checks the light, so cutting green on today's yellow could be the wrong cut. My message confirms the plan, adds the re-read-the-light instruction, and hands over the complete table so no further round-trip through me is needed.

Answering the four questions out of the manual: the display appears nowhere in it — reading 0 requires nothing, it is inert. The keypad rule is exactly one line: press the key wearing ⵘ, which is position 1, the trident/Y-with-stem key; the printed symbol matters only to identify that key, and no digit code exists in my manual. The wire rule: the light names a single cut, one wire, no order among the three — yellow light cuts green (third), red light cuts red (first), blue light cuts yellow (second). Nothing else changes it: not the display, not the keypad beyond that one press. Any light outside the three rows — white, black, unlit — is not covered: hold and ask me. Touch discipline stays as established: before the press, nothing but the key-1 press; cutting is only sanctioned after it.

Encoding for Deaf in their code: confirm, then "press keypad key 1, release — then the light", the three rows, the hold-and-ask fallback, "display: ignore", "keypad: nothing further", and a closing 🤝 authorising Deaf and Blind to finish on the post-press light without waiting for me again.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "✋", "👊", "🖖", "👆", "🤚", "🫰", "👎", "✊", "👋", "👌", "👈", "👍", "✊", "👋", "👍", "👆", "☝", "✊", "👋", "👎", "👇", "🤟", "✌", "✋", "🤙", "🫰", "🤞", "✋", "🖖", "✋", "🤝"])
```

Intended reading for Deaf: "Confirmed, your reading is correct. Attention. Press keypad key 1, release. Then the light names the cut: yellow light → cut green wire, third wire; red light → cut red wire, first wire; blue light → cut yellow wire, second wire. White or black light → hold, ask me about the light. Display: ignore it, the manual never mentions it. Keypad: nothing further after the press. Agreed — proceed on the post-press light."

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Blind says to Mute: Blind reporting. I received Deaf's relay and carried it out exactly: one firm full press on the leftmost key, position one, pressed and released, hands completely off the bomb now — nothing else touched, all wires intact. I signed fist to Deaf before touching and thumbs-up after letting go. The complete tactile report — any click, snap, hum or vibration from the press — I will state at the start of next round, because the full result of the press reaches me when my hands' view updates, and Deaf will see what the display and light do and can report that too. Until Deaf names an exact wire by position, I am not cutting anything.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decoded your message: you confirmed my reading, and you repeated the instruction press key 1 and release — that is ALREADY DONE. Blind pressed it last round, the bomb announced the keypad opens, and the keypad now shows one digit entered, the digit 1. Answering your question: the light is still yellow, the display is still 0, and the keypad module has opened. Your rule list as I read it: light yellow means cut the green wire; the other branches mention red, blue, white and black cases that cannot apply to our bomb, since our wires are red, yellow, green. The yellow branch is the only one that fits, and our light IS yellow. I am holding Blind one round away from the cut. Give the final order now: gesture the cut symbol for green — fist, wave, fingers making a circle — and Blind cuts immediately next round. If anything about the opened keypad changes the rule, gesture hold instead and explain.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝 👊 🖖 👆 🤚 🙌 🫰 👎 🤞 🫵 🤙 ✊ 👋 👌]

The chain in the manual is now satisfied up to its final link: the ⵘ key (position 1) was pressed and released, the bomb answered, and the post-press light reads yellow — confirmed stable across both of Deaf's reports. The yellow row names the cut: the green wire, which sits at position 3, rightmost of three. That is the whole rule; nothing waits on the display (the manual never mentions it, 0 requires nothing) and nothing waits on the keypad (opened or not, no digit entry appears anywhere in my manual — the single press already fulfilled its only clause, and the "1 entered" is just residue of that press). So the opened keypad changes nothing, and I answer Deaf's question rather than holding.

Deaf's summary contained one small garble — they called the red/blue/white/black branches inapplicable "since our wires are red, yellow, green," when in fact the blue branch cuts a wire we do have (yellow, position 2). It's moot while the light is yellow, and I spelled out all three rows with positions last round, so I won't reopen the table and risk confusing the final order; the operative branch is decoded identically by all three of us. Cutting is sanctioned now: the press is done, so this touch is no longer "while it waits."

I send the exact confirmation Deaf asked for — cut green — plus the position digit for redundancy, and the done sign so Blind knows nothing follows the cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "✊", "👋", "👌", "👈", "🙌"])
```

Intended reading for Deaf to relay: "Confirmed, your reading is correct and the opened keypad changes nothing. Cut the green wire — position 3, rightmost. After the cut, we are done; no further action, ignore display and keypad."

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind report, as asked. What I felt when the keypad opened: the key at position one travelled down and clicked once at the bottom, then sprang back up cleanly. No hum, no vibration, no snap, no panel swinging loose, nothing new appeared under my hands afterwards — the bomb feels exactly as before, just with that one press registered. Note that the digit now entered is printed, so its value is invisible to me; Deaf is the one who can read it. Second task done: I traced the wires carefully from the far left and counted one, two, three. The third wire, the rightmost one, is located and I have it fixed by position and thickness. I cut nothing, pressed nothing, and my hands are fully clear of the bomb now — I signed fist while tracing and thumbs-up once located. I act next only on Deaf's explicit order naming the wire and the cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decoded your order: confirm, cut the green wire, the third wire, done. The order is being given to Blind right now and the cut happens this round. One thing you should have on your radar: the display still reads 0 and the keypad shows one digit entered. If the manual says anything happens after the wires — display input, holding a button, anything with the opened keypad or the light — prepare that step and send it next round. Question about the display: does the 0 mean anything per the manual?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝 ✊ 👋 👌 👈 🤙 🤞]

The manual is exhausted — there is nothing after the cut. It contains exactly two clauses: the first press (done) and the light naming one cut (being executed now). No display rule, no keypad rule, no post-wire step exists anywhere in it, so the answer to Deaf's question is a firm "nothing": the display appears nowhere in the manual, and 0 requires nothing. Preparing any follow-on step would mean inventing a rule that isn't there — the only safe instruction is that the procedure ends with the green wire, and that anything unexpected triggers a hold-and-report instead of improvisation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "🤞", "✋", "🖖", "✋", "🫰", "✋", "🙌", "✋", "🙏"])
```

Intended reading for Deaf: "Acknowledged. Display: nothing — the manual never mentions a display; 0 requires nothing. Keypad: nothing further — no digit input or held button exists in the manual, opened or not. Light: once it names the cut, nothing further. Done — the procedure is complete the moment the green wire is cut; there is no step after the wires. If anything unexpected happens — the light or display changing, anything new under Blind's hands — hold, touch nothing, and report to me first."
